subject.title: fix(memory): exclude extraPaths from shared scope hash to avoid unnecessary reindexing

question: Should same-workspace builtin memory become a default shared SQLite store, and what migration, session-visibility, manager-lifecycle, and SDK contract must that design use?
rationale: The patch changes shipped persistent storage and cross-agent/session visibility boundaries, so automation cannot choose the product and security model safely.

options.title: Require shared-store design before merge
options.body: Keep the branch open or paused until maintainers accept a complete design with migration/rebuild handling, store-scoped lifecycle, session filtering, and SDK contract tests.

options.title: Accept the workspace-shared boundary
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly choose same-workspace sharing as the access boundary, but the PR must then own upgrade proof, CLI/tool visibility consistency, and public API compatibility.

options.title: Narrow to extraPaths identity only
options.body: Drop the default shared database and registry exports, then solve only the extraPaths reindex identity problem within the existing per-agent store model.

recommendation.title: Require shared-store design before merge
recommendation.body: Keep the branch open or paused until maintainers accept a complete design with migration/rebuild handling, store-scoped lifecycle, session filtering, and SDK contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses memory product behavior, plugin SDK shape, and session visibility, and steipete has the broadest feature-history signal across these files.
